member.name: T:Microsoft.VisualBasic.Drawing.DirectX.DxCanvas
member.summary: A winforms control that draws its whole content through the gpu accelerated directx 2d pipeline.
member.remarks:
The control owns a dxgi flip model swap chain that is bound to its own window handle, so the winform paint cycle drives the gpu presentation directly:
1. opens a drawing frame on the swap chain 2. the event is raised, the handler draws through the IGraphics of the event data 3. finishes the frame and presents it onto the window
The control never paints through gdi+ - the gpu canvas owns every pixel of the client area - so the background painting is suppressed and the opaque style is set, which removes the flickering frame of a gdi+ filled control.
The canvas is recreated together with the window handle, so docking, re-parenting and a dpi change are handled transparently. A removed gpu device is handled by the backend itself: the swap chain is rebuilt at the beginning of the next frame.

member.name: T:Microsoft.VisualBasic.Drawing.DirectX.DxScene3DCanvas
member.summary: A winforms canvas that renders an interactive 3d scene through the gpu accelerated directx pipeline.
member.remarks:
This control is the winforms adapter of the reusable 3d scene pipeline of the Microsoft.VisualBasic.Drawing.DirectX.Scene3D namespace:
* the scene geometry is owned by * the view interaction is owned by * the lighting is owned by * the rendering is done by an . The default back end is the real direct3d 11 pipeline (): the geometry is uploaded once and every frame only a constant buffer and a handful of draw calls are sent to the gpu device. renders straight into the canvas back buffer without any copy, and keeps the original polygon painter as the comparison and fall back path.
The control only translates the winforms mouse and keyboard events into the neutral input model of the controller and requests a repaint afterwards, so the whole pipeline stays reusable outside of winforms.
Input mapping: the left button orbits the camera, the right button translates the view, the mouse wheel changes the view distance.
